title: Containers: AKS vs Container Apps
description: Compare Azure Kubernetes Service and Azure Container Apps to decide which container platform fits your workload.

data.text: **Containers** package an application and its dependencies into a single, portable unit. Azure offers two main services for running containers: **Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)** and **Azure Container Apps**. Each has a different level of control and operational complexity.

AKS is a managed Kubernetes service. Kubernetes is an open-source system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. With AKS, Azure manages the Kubernetes control plane, but you still manage the worker nodes, networking, and cluster configuration.

Azure Container Apps is a serverless container service. You do not manage Kubernetes or virtual machines. You define your container image, scaling rules, and environment variables, and Azure runs them for you.

cards.title: AKS
cards.description: Managed Kubernetes for full control over container orchestration.
pros: Full Kubernetes feature set and ecosystem
Fine-grained control over networking and security

cards.title: Container Apps
pros: Pay for what you use with consumption pricing
cons: Not ideal for very large, complex clusters

data.title: Quick Decision Guide
items: **Choose AKS** if your team already uses Kubernetes or needs advanced orchestration features.
**Choose Container Apps** if you want to run containers without managing infrastructure.
**Choose App Service** if you just need to run code and do not care about containers.
**Choose Functions** if your workload is event-driven and short-lived.

terms.definition: A lightweight, portable package containing an application and its dependencies.
Azure Kubernetes Service, a managed Kubernetes platform.
A serverless Azure service for running containerized applications.
A service for storing and managing container images.

data.title: Note
data.text: You do not have to choose only one. Many organizations use Container Apps for new projects and AKS for existing Kubernetes workloads.

data.title: Exercise: Match Workloads to Services
data.description: Decide which Azure compute service best fits each scenario.
steps: A team wants to migrate an existing Docker Compose setup to Azure with minimal changes.
A startup needs to run 20 microservices and is already familiar with Kubernetes.
An event-driven workflow that processes messages for a few seconds each.
data.expectedOutcome: You can justify why Container Apps, AKS, or Functions is the best choice for a given workload.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Containers make applications portable and consistent across environments.
AKS provides full Kubernetes control with managed infrastructure.
Container Apps offers serverless containers with minimal management.
Use comparison cards and decision guides to choose the right service.
data.takeaway: Both AKS and Container Apps run containers, but they differ in control, complexity, and operational overhead.
